title: Rating Rule: Permissive-Operator Surcharge on Assigned Repair Payments
content:
**Rule.** Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), a permissive-operator surcharge is added to the deductible an assigned repair payment carries:
- **Collision.** When the operator recorded on the claim report is a permissive user who does not live in the household and the cause is a collision, the permissive-collision surcharge of 500 USD is added.
- **Comprehensive.** When that operator is such a permissive user and the cause is comprehensive, the permissive-comprehensive surcharge of 250 USD is added.
- **Any other operator.** A rated driver, a named excluded driver, an unlisted household resident, or no driver at all brings no surcharge.

### Surcharge by operator and cause (USD)

| Operator standing on the claim report | Collision cause | Comprehensive cause |
|---|---|---|
| Permissive user not living in the household | 500 | 250 |
| Rated driver | None | None |
| Named excluded driver | None | None |
| Unlisted household resident | None | None |
| No driver (parked vehicle) | None | None |

### Hypothetical cases

- A neighbour borrows the car and rear-ends another vehicle. The operator is a permissive user who does not live in the household and the cause is a collision, so 500 USD is added to the deductible.
- The same neighbour hits a deer. That is a comprehensive cause, so 250 USD is added.
- The named insured's own rated spouse is driving in either loss. Nothing is added.
